title: From founding to auction, with the market alongside

events.title: Founded
events.text: Louis Borders, founder of Borders Books, starts the company.

events.title: The Bay Area store opens
events.text: Commercial launch, served from the 340,000 sq ft Oakland center.

events.title: Bechtel contract
events.text: Agreement for the construction of up to 26 more distribution centers over three years.

events.title: $275.0M Series D
events.text: 21.7 million preferred shares, just before the IPO filing.

events.title: George Shaheen becomes CEO
events.text: He leaves the top job at Andersen Consulting.

events.title: IPO at $15
events.text: 25 million shares on Nasdaq as WBVN, $375M gross. Goldman Sachs leads.

events.title: $34 high
events.text: The stock's high in its first quarter of trading.

events.title: The Nasdaq peaks
events.text: The index closes at 5,048.62, its bubble high.

events.title: Atlanta opens
events.text: A 350,000 sq ft center in Suwanee, Georgia.

events.title: Chicago opens
events.text: A 355,000 sq ft center in Carol Stream, Illinois.

events.title: HomeGrocer merger closes
events.text: 138.3M new shares; about $1.04B total, $901.6M of it goodwill.

events.title: Low of $0.28
events.text: The stock trades between $2.28 and $0.28 in the quarter.

events.title: Dallas closes
events.text: The ex-HomeGrocer Carrollton, Texas facility shuts. Louis Borders leaves the board.

events.title: Sacramento dropped
events.text: Service ends there too.

events.title: Shaheen resigns
events.text: COO Robert Swan takes over, and is named CEO on Apr 26.

events.title: Atlanta closes
events.text: About 485 jobs there and 400 at headquarters. Cash is down to $115M. A 1-for-25 reverse split is planned.

events.title: Shutdown
events.text: All deliveries stop in seven markets. About 2,000 workers are let go and 750,000 active customers lose the service.

events.title: Chapter 11
events.text: Filed in Delaware, case 01-2404, to pursue a sale of the assets.

events.title: The auctions
events.text: Court-approved auctions at ten facility sites and headquarters.

events.title: The name returns
events.text: Amazon is reported to own webvan.com and uses it to sell groceries by mail.

events.title: Kiva sold to Amazon
events.text: $775M for the robotics company founded by ex-Webvan logistics manager Mick Mountz.
